channel.title: The Tanzania Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Tanzania Times (tanzaniatimes.net)

item.title: Don’t Let History Repeat Itself in the 21st Century
item.description: Not in abstract figures, but in lived reality: homes in ruins, mass graves, and families driven from everything they knew. The images are horrendous and shocking to watch.

item.title: The Man Who Became Myth: How Chuck Norris Shaped a Generation Beyond the Screen!
item.description: To write about Norris is not to chronicle an actor’s career; it is to interrogate the anatomy of influence itself, how a man forged in modest beginnings became a global emblem of resilience, justice, and cultural mythology.

item.title: Tuberculosis causes 85,000 deaths from 920,000 new cases in the Eastern Mediterranean Region
item.description: Between 2020 to 2024, over 2.8 million TB cases were diagnosed and successfully treated – treatment success rates exceeded 90 percent– contributing to a significant reduction in the TB burden

item.title: Libya’s Ministry of Defense secures the Russian Ghost Ship, Artic Metagaz, onto a tugboat before disaster
item.description: A team from the Libyan Ministry of Defense successfully boarded the damaged Russian LNG tanker Arctic Metagaz and managed to secure it to a tugboat dispatched from the port of Misrata.

item.title: Elon Musk thrown out of Namibia, attempting to offer the country Internet Services through his Starlink
item.description: Elon Musk’s attempts to start providing direct to satellite internet services in Namibia have been thwarted by local authorities.Reports from Windhoek reveal that the Communications Regulatory Authority of Namibia (CRAN) has declined the application

item.title: Marine Flyways: A Major Breakthrough in Global Ocean Conservation
item.description: Marine flyways are vast migration highways across the open ocean, used by more than 150 seabird species across 54 countries.

item.title: Beyond the First Drop: The Alchemy of Crude and the Moral Reckoning of Uganda’s Oil Age!
item.description: Production forecasts of between 190,000 and 230,000 barrels per day at peak translate into potential revenues running into billions of dollars over the lifecycle of the fields.

item.title: When the Strait of Hormuz closes, Africa pays first
item.description: Countries like Kenya, Tanzania, Ethiopia and Zambia are already implementing emergency measures, including subsidies and reserve releases.

item.title: Flood disaster in Kenya renews debate on climate risk and preparedness
item.description: Since the start of March, parts of Nairobi, Nyakach and surrounding regions have been hit by heavy rainfall that destroyed homes, swept away crops and forced families to flee low-lying areas

item.title: CityBlue Hotels now Launching Diani Beach Residences in Kenya
item.description: Set on approximately five acres, the project is envisioned as a flagship lifestyle destination comprising between 400 and 500 contemporary residential units

item.title: Why the Future of Customs is Agentic Artificial Intelligence
item.description: Administrations that embrace agentic AI will see faster clearance, higher revenue protection, and, most importantly, operational autonomy

item.title: Thomson’s first historical encounter with the Maasai in East Africa
item.description: The Maasai had a reputation across East Africa that was almost mythical, other communities spoke of them as warriors who feared nothing, not even death.

item.title: United States Secretary of Energy Chris Wright says clean cooking is key to Africa policy
item.description: Clean cooking means moving away from solid fuels such as wood and charcoal that have proven health risks to more modern energy sources

item.title: Dangote Petroleum Refinery gets USD 2.5 from the African Export-Import Bank
item.description: Afreximbank and Access Bank were appointed co-Mandated Lead Arrangers for the five-year facility to consolidate existing financing, optimize its capital structure and align with the refinery’s operational status

item.title: Radisson Hotel Group Surpasses 100 Hotels in Africa, Accelerating 2030 Growth Ambition
item.description: Radisson Hotel Group also plans to enter the Zanzibar Islands of Tanzania, where it intends to set up a luxury lodge and Safari outfit.
